research.summary: Data-center accelerator demand remains the primary revenue driver, with public disclosures showing continued sequential growth.
research.thesis: Sustained hyperscaler capex on AI accelerators supports multi-year demand for the company's data-center GPU platform.
research.counterThesis: Customer concentration among a handful of hyperscalers, combined with rising internal-silicon efforts at those same customers, could compress long-run demand and pricing power.
risks: Export-control changes could restrict addressable market in key regions.
Two customers account for a large share of disclosed data-center revenue.
unknowns: Next-generation platform yield rates have not been publicly disclosed.
falsifiers: A sustained multi-quarter sequential decline in data-center segment revenue.
Public confirmation that a top-two customer has materially cut multi-year orders.

sources.title: Independent analysis of hyperscaler capex trends

research.summary: Memory pricing has firmed on constrained supply and AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory.
research.thesis: A multi-year memory upcycle, driven in part by HBM demand, supports margin expansion.
research.counterThesis: Memory markets are historically cyclical; a supply response from competitors could compress pricing sooner than the base case assumes.
risks: Commodity memory pricing is historically volatile and cyclical.
unknowns: Competitor capacity-expansion timelines are not fully public.
falsifiers: A sustained decline in spot DRAM or NAND pricing over consecutive quarters.
